title: Stored version, public endpoint, and automated Git tags
description:
What it is
Add a repo-level backend release identity for Compass BE that is stored in a committed root VERSION file, exposed by a public NestJS endpoint, reused by Swagger/OpenAPI, and advanced/tagged automatically in GitHub Actions on deploy-triggering branch pushes.

Why it exists
Operational visibility — operators should be able to confirm the live backend release from HTTP, similar to the existing public GET /health endpoint, without SSHing into EC2 or inspecting PM2.

Single source of truth — the release semver should live in one committed file in the repo instead of being split across code, tags, and deploy metadata.

Traceable deploys — Git tags should point to commits that actually contain the released VERSION value.

Branch-aware diagnostics — the running app should report both the deployed Git SHA and the branch that scripts/ec2_deploy.sh checked out on the instance.

Future per-version storage — benchmarks, test runs, coverage, and other metrics can be keyed by a stable backend version string.

Codebase context
Compass BE is a NestJS backend. It already exposes public endpoints from src/app.controller.ts, already has Swagger configured in src/main.ts, and already deploys through .github/workflows/deploy.yml into EC2 via scripts/ec2_deploy.sh and PM2. This story should extend that existing flow rather than introduce a parallel release mechanism.

Implementation and testing expectations
- All changes must follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md.
- All new behavior introduced by this story must be covered according to docs/TESTING.md.
- New NestJS code should keep controllers thin, centralize business logic in reusable services/utilities, and include explicit Swagger decorators and DTO documentation where applicable.
- Public API changes must include or update e2e coverage.
- New controller/service/utility code should include focused unit tests with mocked dependencies and atomic test cases.
- Release bump/tag automation and deploy metadata logic should include automated verification where feasible; where full end-to-end automation is impractical, the implementation must still isolate logic enough to verify key paths such as patch bumping, idempotency, and feature-branch no-op behavior.

Scope
1. Add a committed root VERSION file
- Create VERSION at repo root containing a full semantic version string like 1.4.23.
- This file becomes the canonical runtime/backend version source.
- Developers may override any semver component by editing VERSION directly and committing the change.
- package.json version is informational for now; VERSION is the canonical source unless a later follow-up enforces alignment.

2. Expose a public GET /version endpoint
- Add an unauthenticated endpoint alongside the existing public app endpoints.
- Response should include:
  - version: semantic version from root VERSION
  - gitSha: full SHA
  - gitShaShort: short SHA
  - branch: deployed branch
- Endpoint should be safe for dev/staging/prod and remain available after npm run build + PM2 restart on EC2.

3. Resolve runtime version metadata inside the Nest app
- The app should read the semver from root VERSION.
- Because production runs compiled output from dist/, implementation must explicitly support this repo's runtime layout.
- Preferred approaches to evaluate in code:
  - read from repo root using a deterministic path relative to process.cwd() / compiled files, or
  - copy VERSION into build output via Nest assets if root-path assumptions are brittle.
- The implementation should be centralized in one reusable service/utility rather than duplicated across controller and bootstrap.

4. Pass Git SHA and branch through deploy runtime env
- scripts/ec2_deploy.sh already knows the branch being deployed and can resolve git rev-parse HEAD.
- Update deploy/runtime startup so PM2 injects env vars for branch and SHA into the running Nest process.
- GET /version should use these runtime values rather than shelling out to Git on every request.

5. Align Swagger/OpenAPI version with runtime version
- Replace the hardcoded Swagger version in src/main.ts.
- Swagger should display the same semver returned by GET /version.

6. Add automated release bump + tag workflow in GitHub Actions
- Extend the existing GitHub Actions setup without breaking current OIDC-based EC2 deploy permissions.
- On pushes to dev, staging, and main only:
  - read VERSION,
  - bump patch by default,
  - commit the updated VERSION as a dedicated release commit,
  - create tag v<version> on that commit,
  - push commit and tag.
- Developers can still override major/minor/patch manually by editing VERSION before pushing.
- The workflow must be idempotent:
  - if the branch tip is already the tagged release commit for the current VERSION, skip.
- Feature branches (feature/**) must not create semver release tags.

7. Document branch and merge behaviour
- dev -> staging -> main merges carry the VERSION file forward.
- The branch returned by GET /version reflects the branch checked out by scripts/ec2_deploy.sh on that server.
- Document developer workflow for:
  - manual semver override by editing VERSION,
  - normal automated release bumping on deploy branches,
  - non-tagging policy for feature branches.

Acceptance criteria
- A root VERSION file exists and stores full semver in major.minor.patch format.
- Version format and developer override workflow are documented in docs/AUTO_DEPLOYMENT.md or a dedicated versioning doc.
- Compass BE exposes public GET /version returning version, full SHA, short SHA, and branch.
- Runtime SHA/branch come from deploy/runtime env set during scripts/ec2_deploy.sh execution.
- Swagger/OpenAPI reports the same version string as GET /version.
- GitHub Actions automatically creates a dedicated release commit and matching Git tag on pushes to dev, staging, and main.
- The tag points to the commit whose VERSION file matches the tag.
- Re-running the workflow on an already released branch tip does not create duplicate release commits or tags.
- Feature branches do not receive semver release tags.
- New version-resolution logic and public endpoint behavior are covered by automated tests consistent with docs/TESTING.md.
- Public API changes include e2e coverage.
- Changes follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md, including explicit Swagger annotations for any new endpoint DTOs/responses.

features.title: Backend version source and runtime resolver
features.description:
Create a committed root VERSION file as the canonical backend semver source for Compass BE. Implement a shared NestJS resolver/service/utility that reads and validates VERSION for runtime use, supports the compiled dist runtime layout used on EC2, and defines safe behavior for missing or invalid version data. package.json version remains informational for now; VERSION is canonical.

Implementation notes
- Follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md by keeping file reading/parsing logic centralized and reusable rather than duplicating it across bootstrap and controllers.
- If new DTOs, interfaces, or config/env variables are introduced, place and document them according to repo standards.

Testing expectations
- Add focused unit tests alongside the resolver/service/utility file per docs/TESTING.md.
- Cover valid VERSION parsing, invalid format handling, missing file behavior, and runtime path resolution assumptions.
- Keep tests atomic and mock filesystem/process dependencies where practical.

features.title: Public GET /version endpoint
features.description:
Add an unauthenticated public endpoint in the NestJS app that returns the backend release identity for operators and diagnostics. Response should include version from VERSION, full git SHA, short git SHA, and deployed branch. Place it alongside the existing public app endpoints.

Implementation notes
- Follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md by keeping the controller thin and moving response-building logic into a reusable service.
- Use explicit Swagger decorators on the route and DTO properties if a response DTO is introduced.

Testing expectations
- Add focused controller/service unit tests with mocked dependencies per docs/TESTING.md.
- Add or update e2e coverage for the public API contract because this story introduces a new public endpoint.
- Cover the exact response shape, public accessibility, and representative metadata values, with atomic happy-path/error-path tests where applicable.

features.title: Swagger/OpenAPI version alignment
features.description:
Replace the hardcoded Swagger version in src/main.ts and make OpenAPI use the same resolved semantic version source as the runtime /version endpoint.

Implementation notes
- Follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md by reusing the centralized version-resolution logic rather than introducing parallel bootstrap-only behavior.
- Preserve explicit Swagger/OpenAPI annotations and existing docs behavior.

Testing expectations
- Add focused automated verification that Swagger/OpenAPI is initialized with the same semantic version returned by the shared resolver.
- Prefer a unit or bootstrap-level test over manual verification where practical.
- Keep assertions atomic and avoid coupling the test to unrelated Swagger configuration.

features.title: Deploy runtime metadata injection via ec2_deploy.sh
features.description:
Update scripts/ec2_deploy.sh and the PM2 startup/reload flow so the running NestJS process receives deploy metadata as runtime environment variables, specifically deployed branch and git SHA. The /version endpoint should consume these env vars instead of shelling out to git on each request.

Implementation notes
- Follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md by keeping deploy metadata handling deterministic and avoiding duplicated branch/SHA resolution logic.
- Prefer a single documented env contract for the Nest runtime rather than ad hoc shell lookups.

Testing expectations
- Add automated verification for the metadata propagation logic where feasible, for example by isolating shell/script decision logic into testable units or validating generated runtime env inputs.
- Cover branch and SHA propagation, PM2 restart/reload behavior assumptions, and failure/no-op paths as practical.
- If some EC2/PM2 behavior cannot be fully automated, document the manual verification steps explicitly in the implementation notes or docs.

features.title: Automated release bump and Git tagging workflow
features.description:
Extend the existing GitHub Actions release/deploy flow so pushes to dev, staging, and main read VERSION, bump patch by default, create a dedicated release commit updating VERSION, tag that commit as v<version>, and push both commit and tag. Preserve existing OIDC deploy behavior, make the workflow idempotent when the branch tip is already the tagged release commit, and ensure feature/** branches do not create semver release tags.

Implementation notes
- Follow docs/CODE_STANDARD.md by isolating release decision logic into a reusable script or utility rather than embedding all semantics directly in workflow YAML.
- Keep the workflow deterministic and explicit about branch handling, release commit messages, and tag creation conditions.

Testing expectations
- Add automated verification for patch bumping, manual-version override compatibility, idempotency, and feature-branch no-op behavior.
- Prefer extracting bump/tag decision logic into a testable script so docs/TESTING.md can be satisfied with focused unit/integration-style tests instead of relying only on manual workflow runs.
- Where full GitHub Actions end-to-end testing is impractical, test the underlying logic and document any remaining manual verification steps.

features.title: Versioning and release workflow documentation
features.description:
Document the VERSION file format, developer override workflow, automated release bump behavior, merge flow from dev to staging to main, feature-branch non-tagging policy, and the meaning of branch/SHA values exposed by /version. Update docs/AUTO_DEPLOYMENT.md or add a dedicated versioning doc as appropriate.

Implementation notes
- Keep the documentation aligned with docs/CODE_STANDARD.md terminology and the actual repo paths, workflow names, and deploy scripts.
- Include explicit verification steps for developers and operators where behavior depends on deploy/runtime state.

Testing expectations
- Document what is covered by automated tests versus manual verification for this story.
- Include the expected verification workflow for VERSION changes, /version behavior, and release/tag outcomes so future contributors can validate changes consistently.
